transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-20
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lina Patel (Redwood Solutions), Sara Kim (Atlas Head of ML), Rajiv Menon (Atlas Platform), Priya Shah (Atlas Security)

Summary (auto):
Quick sign-off on POC success criteria and acceptance tests; agree benchmarks, workload sizing, reporting format, and timeline for a 4-week PoC. Action items and SOW to be shared.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we wanted to run through the success criteria and make sure we're aligned for the PoC scope, timeline, and acceptance tests. sounds good?
[00:12] Sara Kim: yep that's perfect. we want this to be a very pragmatic test — specifically focusing on latency, cost, and hallucination rate on our clinical summarization flow.
[00:22] Diego Ruiz: great. quick intro from our side — i'm diego, i'll be running the benchmarks and helping with infra bits. lina will help with eval frameworks.
[00:30] Rajiv Menon: quick context: Atlas runs a nightly ingest pipeline and a near-real-time summarization service used by clinician workflows. expected peak is about 120 rps across the cluster, average session 3 prompts. we want to validate both latency and throughput at realistic concurrency.
[00:50] Priya Shah: and from security we need to confirm data at rest and in-transit encryption, KMS integration, and that logs/audit trail are accessible for compliance. also data residency — all data must remain in our us-east-1 tenancy.
[01:05] Maya Chen: absolutely, we'll include KMS options and the private deployment checklist. ok success criteria — we proposed the following go/no-go thresholds, please interrupt if any of these don't match your expectations.
[01:15] Diego Ruiz: (shares screen) i'm putting them up. Success criteria draft: 1) Latency p95 for single-request summarization <= 250ms for short notes (<512 tokens) and <= 600ms for long notes (~2k tokens). 2) Throughput: sustain 120 rps for 5 minutes with tail-latency p95 < 1s. 3) Quality: hallucination rate < 2% on clinical facts measured by our eval set; F1/ROUGE style metrics to be reported. 4) Cost target: average per-1M-token inference cost that meets your internal target (we flagged $45/1M tokens as target for the POC baseline). 5) Security: KMS-backed encryption, SOC2 documentation provided, and ability to run in your VPC or Dedicated cluster. 6) Stability: zero crashes and acceptable error rate (<0.5% failed requests) during run.
[02:05] Sara Kim: the latency numbers look generally okay but 250ms p95 might be optimistic for some of the longer context cases — but i see you have separate buckets. for the hallucination metric, how are you measuring that?
[02:18] Lina Patel: good question. we'll run an automated evaluator on your labeled subset (we ask you for ~500 labeled summaries). metric is proportion of outputs with one or more clinically incorrect statements per sample; we'll also surface exact examples.
[02:32] Priya Shah: for security, we need to see the SOC2 report and the KMS integration design. can you provide an architecture diagram for private deployment and network egress controls?
[02:44] Maya Chen: yes, we'll share the security pack link — it's the SOC2 + data flow diagrams and KMS integration notes. we'll include the private deployment diagram showing VPC peering, NAT config, and no public egress by default.
[02:56] Rajiv Menon: on workload sizing: we're giving you a sample workload of 5k anonymized patient notes to start; these represent the 95th percentile size distribution. we also want you to run a separate synthetic stress test to 300 rps to observe scaling behavior.
[03:12] Diego Ruiz: ok we'll set up two benchmark phases: baseline (replay your 5k dataset at production concurrency) and stress (synthetic ramp to 300 rps for short intervals). baseline will measure latency, throughput, cost-per-token, and quality. stress will measure stability and autoscaling behavior.
[03:28] Sara Kim: what about reporting format? we prefer a single consolidated report with raw logs, aggregates (p50/p95/p99), cost breakdown, failure traces, and a short executive summary with go/no-go recommendation.
[03:40] Lina Patel: we can deliver that. our standard deliverable is a Google Sheet with raw sample-level outputs, a PDF exec summary, and a CSV of traces. we can also upload a small dashboard link for interactive exploration.
[03:52] Priya Shah: timeline?
[03:55] Maya Chen: proposed: Week 0 (this week) - finalize SOW and access; Week 1 - onboarding and infra prep; Week 2 - baseline benchmarks on your dataset; Week 3 - optimizations (batching, quantization variants as appropriate); Week 4 - final acceptance run and report + sign-off. total ~4 weeks.
[04:12] Rajiv Menon: that's tight but doable. we need clear triggers for success. what's the exact go/no-go decision rule?
[04:19] Diego Ruiz: suggested go/no-go: at acceptance run, if 4 of the 6 primary criteria (latency bucket, throughput, quality, cost target, security requirements met, stability) meet thresholds, we pass. if fewer than 4 pass, it's a no-go and we document remediation steps. for costs, if cost is slightly above target but can be improved via quantization within Week 3 without degrading quality, we treat that as 'conditional pass'.
[04:43] Sara Kim: that seems reasonable. can we add an absolute block: if hallucination > 5% or any PII leakage observed, immediate stop?
[04:51] Priya Shah: yes, security is hard stop.
[04:54] Maya Chen: agreed — hallucination > 5% or evidence of PII leakage is automatic fail. we'll include tests for PII leakage in the evaluation harness.
[05:02] Rajiv Menon: and for reporting cadence, we'd like a mid-week checkpoint after baseline (a lightweight dashboard) and then a final report.
[05:09] Lina Patel: noted. we'll provide an interim report after baseline run within 48 hours.
[05:13] Maya Chen: ok i want to call out a few concrete acceptance tests we'll run during the final acceptance run: 1) Run the 5k dataset at production concurrency for 30 minutes — measure p95 latency buckets and error rate. 2) Run 3 adversarial prompts per 100 samples to test hallucination and PII heuristics. 3) Run synthetic ramp to verify autoscaling to 300 rps for 2 minutes with tail-latency under 2s. 4) Verify KMS integration by encrypting test artifacts and confirming key access logs. 5) Cost calc: reproduce cost breakdown for the acceptance run and compare to target.
[05:44] Sara Kim: sounds good. please make sure the evaluator flags example outputs with clinical detail so our SMEs can review.
[05:50] Diego Ruiz: we will export an examples file. small note — transcription: some proper nouns in our notes may get changed in the quick eval but the raw outputs are preserved.
[05:58] Rajiv Menon: about deployment mode — if the hosted API hits a security blocker we'll plan for Dedicated or Private (VPC) deployment. what's the lead time for Private?
[06:08] Maya Chen: for Private it's typically 4-6 weeks for full provisioning with network setup; Dedicated is faster, usually 1-2 weeks. however for the POC we can run the initial benchmarks on our hosted infra within your VPC peering or via temporary secure tunnel if needed.
[06:22] Priya Shah: temporary tunnel is okay as long as we can validate egress controls.
[06:26] Maya Chen: noted. ok to summarize next steps — Maya to send SOW and pricing, Diego to prepare benchmark harness, Atlas to provide dataset and constraints, Priya to confirm KMS requirements. we'll schedule the baseline run for 2025-10-27.
[06:40] Sara Kim: agreed. thanks everyone.
[06:43] Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up via email and add action items to the SOW.
[06:47] (call ends)

Attachments/References: Security pack link (shared in chat): https://redwood.example.com/security-pack/atlas-2025; PoC SOW template link; Benchmark harness repo link (private).

Recorded decisions / Acceptance thresholds (quick list):
- Latency: p95 <=250ms (short), <=600ms (long)
- Throughput: sustain 120 rps with p95 <1s; autoscale to 300 rps for stress
- Quality: hallucination <2% (auto eval); immediate fail if >5% or PII leakage
- Cost: target <= $45 per 1M tokens (conditional pass allowed with clear remediation)
- Security: KMS + SOC2 docs and private deployment options satisfied
- Stability: error rate <0.5% during run

End of transcript.
